items.title: Angela Stanley President and CEO of Groves Memorial Community
notes: Hospital and Alison Armstrong, Manager, Communications, Stakeholder Relations and Physician Recruitment, Groves Memorial Community Hospital
re: Groves Memorial Community Hospital - Year in Review Angela Stanley outlined the growth and increased activity in the three communities, Wellington North, Minto-Mapleton and Centre Wellington.
She highlighted the 174 new staff hired since April, 2024, including 72 nurses and the new installation of the CT scanner on March 4, 2025.

Alison Armstrong provided an overview of the physician recruitment initiatives and thanked staff and Council for their continued partnership and support for the hospital and healthcare professional recruitment efforts.

items.title: County Councillor Mary Lloyd provided an update on the closing of the
notes: Elora transfer station on April 5th for renovations, the success of the automated speed enforcement, the highway 109 road improvements that will impact traffic flow and the farming community, the continuation of the winter response program for the homeless, successful March break programs at the various libraries, and the potential regulation of Escooters.

items.title: Councillor's Committee Updates
notes: Members of Council provided updates on the activities of Safe Communities, the Economic Prosperity & Growth Committee and Farm Safety.

items.title: Consent Items
notes: Mayor Watters indicated the Consent Agenda Items are considered routine in nature and are voted on collectively. However, any Member of Council may request one or more items be removed from the Consent Agenda for separate action.
Gerry Atkinson, Manager of Waste Water Services provided additional details on the bypass issues and mechanical upgrades implemented.

items.title: Community Investment Fund Recipient Recommendation
notes: Report from K. Bettiol, Manager of Community Development K. Bettiol, Manager of Community Development provided an overview of the report, indicating the community investment fund is to provide financial assistance to enhance the quality of life by fostering, strengthening and stimulating wider community appreciation and participation in the community. She outlined the process undertaken, including the scoring tool used. She highlighted the recipients of the annual specific stream funding in the amount of $23,150 and outlined the eligible recipients for the community impact totalling $56,500.

items.title: Asset Management Levels of Service Framework
notes: Report from A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer

Adam McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer provided an overview of the report, indicating staff have been working in concert with SLBC to develop a Levels of Service (LOS) framework that would be compliant with legislation and facilitate the long-term service delivery target setting for Centre Wellington.

Eric Goforth, Senior Associate, Advisory Services, SLBC Inc., provided an overview of the proposed framework and outlined the three phases of the project; Phase 1 develop the Levels of Service framework, Phase 2 Community Engagement Strategy and Phase 3 Proposed LOS and Implementation Plan. He outlined the Levels of Service Approach, the project outcomes, and the next steps in the project.

E. Goforth responded to questions regarding the historical performance of the measures tracked, adjustment of the long-term metrix within the framework, staff resources required to maintain, and use of the marketing framework and graphics for community engagement.
Councillor Wilton, having declared a conflict of interest left the meeting and did not participate in any discussions nor did she vote on the matter.

items.title: Municipal Endorsement of County of Wellington OPA 126
notes: Report from B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development

B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development provided an overview of the report and highlighted the modifications, the requested commentary on policy modifications and ongoing requests to add additional parcels to the settlement area.
He responded to questions regarding the solution for the landlocked parcels, the Minimum Distance Separation (MDS) impact, and the minor rounding out of lands within Elora.

items.title: Response to September 16th Community Delegation From Segal
notes: Construction Regarding Attainable Housing
Report from B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development

B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development provided an overview of the report, indicating the delegation from Segal Construction suggested a model for attainable housing using municipal financing which is not feasible. He did, however, provide additional information regarding use of Minister’s Orders. He explained the use of the Minister’s Order as a tool to expedite planning approvals and streamline development.

items.title: 2025 Debt Issue
notes: Report from A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer

Adam McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer noted staff is anticipating the need for marketing a debt issue to satisfy the Township’s long-term borrowing needs for 2025. He indicated staff has investigated three opportunities and is seeking Council direction to proceed with formalizing one of the options outlined in the report.
Adam McNabb responded to a question regarding the impact and potential risk in the event of a reduction or elimination of development charges.
